builder_plan.scenario: A narrow, repeated product task may not need your largest model.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a released student model fits the task before generating training data.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model and an off-the-shelf small model on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Student quality, serving cost, teacher calls, training cost, and failures on unusual inputs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Which Successes Make Good References? Action-Sequence Alignment for Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation
summary: Replaces heuristic or reference-free selection of successful trajectories in multi-turn on-policy distillation with an LCS-based compatibility assignment. Costs additional computation to align action sequences between failed and successful trajectories, but requires no architectural changes or extra model parameters. Can fail when the LCS proxy does not capture true latent state compatibility, leading to misleading supervision from incompatible references.
rationale: The method addresses a specific failure mode in multi-turn OPD with a computationally cheap heuristic, but its effectiveness depends on action-sequence alignment being a valid proxy for state compatibility in the reader's specific domain.
technique: Action-sequence aligned reference selection for on-policy distillation

claims.statement: Replaces heuristic or reference-free selection of successful trajectories in multi-turn on-policy distillation with an LCS-based compatibility assignment. Costs additional computation to align action sequences between failed and successful trajectories, but requires no architectural changes or extra model parameters. Can fail when the LCS proxy does not capture true latent state compatibility, leading to misleading supervision from incompatible references.

LCS is the only evaluated selector that improves over reference-free OPD on both ALFWorld overall scores and all three airline metrics, and it improves all three metrics when transferred to the retail domain.
